subject: Reserved Pool Throughput Annex — tokens/sec guarantees & ramp
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <ops@brightpath.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai, Alice Huang <alice.huang@brightpath.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved Pool Throughput Annex — tokens/sec guarantees & ramp

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, attached is a first-pass annex to cover the reserved-pool throughput guarantee you asked for during renewal. High-level items included:

- Guaranteed baseline: 350 tokens/sec sustained across the reserved pool with 99.5% monthly availability.
- Ramp schedule: 30-day staged ramp from baseline to peak (350 -> 700 tokens/sec) with checkpoints at days 7, 14, and 30 to validate perf and adjust batch sizing.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to compatible model variant at 90th percentile latency breach and temporary credits if we miss SLOs.
- Credit calculation: pro-rata credits capped at 10% of monthly reserved fee per month, calculated on minutes of degraded capacity vs target.
- Operational hooks: weekly throughput review, one technical contact for incident escalation, and a 48-hour remediation SLA for non-degraded capacity issues.

I attached an SLO table showing the proposed measurement windows and the intended telemetry signals (avg tokens/sec, p95 latency, KV cache hit rate). Please have procurement and engineering take a look — flagged items in the PDF are where we expect negotiation (credit cap and remediation timelines).

Next steps I suggest: procurement review + legal redline (we can accept limited exceptions on credits but would like to keep the 30-day ramp and automated fallback language). If that looks okay, we can prep a DocuSign so the annex sits alongside the renewal term.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachments: BrightPath_Renewal_Annex_v1.pdf, Throughput_SLO_Table.xlsx
From: Samir Rao <ops@brightpath.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai, Alice Huang <alice.huang@brightpath.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved Pool Throughput Annex — tokens/sec guarantees & ramp

Neha,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear table. A few items from our side:

1) Baseline vs peak — we need a firm guarantee for production traffic at 500 tokens/sec (not just 350). Can you confirm how the ramp is protected from noisy neighbors during the staging window?

2) Credits — the 10% cap will be tough for finance. Procurement wants an explicit escalation path and a break clause if repeated misses occur over a rolling 3-month window.

3) Measurement — please confirm the telemetry feed we can pull into our monitoring (Prometheus push or a read-only S3 export).

Alice (cc) — can procurement commit to an expedited review timeline if Redwood can accept a 7% credit cap and a 30-day performance cure before a break clause?

Also copying our engineering lead (ops@brightpath.ai) in case you need deeper perf logs.

- Samir
Samir Rao
Head of Platform, BrightPath AI
ops@brightpath.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved Pool Throughput Annex — tokens/sec guarantees & ramp

Neha / Karthik — forwarding Samir's notes. My quick take and suggested edits for the annex:

On noisy neighbors and protection:
- Propose we add an isolation clause for the reserved pool: dedicated GPU affinity for BrightPath during peak windows (2-hour windows configurable) plus enforced tenant cgroups to cap cross-tenant CPU usage. That reduces risk of degraded tokens/sec during ramp.

On credits and break clause:
- We should be willing to move the credit cap to 7% for the first renewal year if BrightPath commits to the 30-day ramp and agreed observability. After year 1, revert to 10% unless they upgrade to a higher tier. For the break clause: require 3 distinct monthly misses where credits exceed 5% to trigger remediation discussions; full contract break only after remediation fails twice.

On telemetry:
- We can offer a read-only S3 export of normalized tokens/sec metrics and a short-lived Prometheus scrape endpoint (10 min TTL) for their monitoring. Legal will want the S3 export language narrow (no PII).

Pricing impact:
- Reducing the cap to 7% increases Redwood's exposure; propose a small one-time implementation fee of $7,500 to cover the dedicated affinity and monitoring exports. Add as line item on renewal quote.

I'll draft redline language for the annex and update the SLO table to include the dedicated affinity windows and the credit calc example. Neha, if you can confirm whether we can accept the 7%/one-time fee offer, I'll prepare the redline and a DocuSign wrapper.

Marissa Cole
Senior Strategic AM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <ops@brightpath.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai, Alice Huang <alice.huang@brightpath.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved Pool Throughput Annex — tokens/sec guarantees & ramp

Samir / Alice — appreciate the quick feedback. Summary of what Redwood can commit to for the renewal annex: 

1) Throughput guarantee: guaranteed baseline of 500 tokens/sec sustained with 99.5% monthly availability; staged ramp remains (30 days to 700 tokens/sec) with checkpoints.

2) Isolation & affinity: we'll add dedicated GPU affinity for configurable 2-hour peak windows and enforce tenant resource caps to protect tokens/sec during ramp.

3) Credits & break clause: initial credit cap of 7% of the monthly reserved fee for the first 12 months; credits calculated pro-rata on minutes below target, capped at 7%. Break clause: triggered only after three months where monthly credits exceed 5% and after two failed remediation cycles.

4) Observability: Redwood will provide a nightly S3 export of normalized tokens/sec and a short-lived Prometheus scrape endpoint during the 30-day ramp. Exports will exclude PII and be retained for 90 days.

5) One-time implementation fee: $7,500 to enable dedicated affinity and monitoring exports (added to the renewal invoice).

If BrightPath can accept those terms we will:
- Marissa will send a redline within 24 hours;
- We will push the annex to DocuSign and aim for signature within 5 business days;
- Technical kickoff with our infra team scheduled within 3 business days of signature.

Samir — are you able to confirm procurement's acceptance of the 7% cap + $7.5k fee? If so we will expedite the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachments referenced: BrightPath_Renewal_Annex_v1.pdf, Throughput_SLO_Table.xlsx
